sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner's name is not found in the FIR.

There is no NC: 2024:KHC:45536 allegation against the petitioner in the FIR or in the statement of the victim girl that was recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C,
On the basis of the statement allegedly made by the victim girl before the Police under Section 161 of Cr.P.C, the petitioner has been arrested.
Even if the said allegation is presumed to be true, the offences alleged in the charge sheet does not get attracted against the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 have strongly opposed the petition.
They submit that the victim girl is a minor, aged about 14 years and therefore the alleged offences get attracted even against the petitioner.
They submit that charge sheet materials are sufficient to connect the petitioner to the crime.
Accordingly, they pray to dismiss the petition.

7. The first informant, who is the younger sister of the victim girl's mother had approached the police and NC: 2024:KHC:45536 submitted a first information on 23.01.2024, based on which, FIR in Crime No.5/2024 was initially registered against five persons.
The mother of the victim girl is arraigned as accused No.5 in the FIR.
The petitioner's name is not found in the FIR.
During the course of investigation, he was arrested on 26.01.2024 and subsequently remanded to judicial custody.
8. The first information was submitted on basis of the information given by the victim girl to the first informant.
It is not in dispute that there is no allegation against the petitioner herein in the first information.
The statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, was recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate on 31.01.2024.
Even in the said statement, the victim girl has not made any allegation against the petitioner and she has not even referred to his name.

9. The statement of the victim girl was recorded by the Police on 25.01.2024 and in the said statement, the victim girl has stated that about 15 days prior to accused NC: 2024:KHC:45536 Nos.1 to 3 sexually assaulted her in a hotel room, she was summoned by accused No.7 (Ramesh), who is the cashier of the said lodge at Shidlaghatta and her mother had sent her to the lodge and in the said lodge, the petitioner herein had sex with her in room No.12.

This allegation found in the statement of the victim girl recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C, is not found either in the first information or in the statement of the victim girl recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
10.

As per the allegation found in the statement of the victim girl under Section 161 of Cr.P.C, that was recorded by the police on 25.01.02024, accused No.7 - Ramesh had summoned the victim girl to the hotel and her mother had sent her to the hotel.
The petitioner, who was a customer had sex with the victim girl in the hotel and he had paid a sum of Rs.1,500/- to her.
Therefore, there is absolutely no material available on record to show that the petitioner had the knowledge that the victim girl was a minor.
The petitioner, who has no other criminal NC: 2024:KHC:45536 antecedents is in custody from 26.01.2024.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the prima-facie opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

12. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in S.C.(POCSO)No.63/2024 pending before the Court of Addl. District & Sessions Judge-FTSC-1, (POCSOA),
Chikkaballapura, arising out of Crime No.5/2024 registered by Chikkaballapura Women Police Station, Chikkaballapura District for the offences punishable under Sections 114, 324, 504, 366(A), 370, 370(A), 370A(1), 370A(2), 376(2)(n), 376(3),
376DA of IPC, Sections 4(2), 6, 17 & 21 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Section 75 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and NC:
2024:KHC:45536 Protection of Children) Act, 2015, Section 3(1)(w) & 3(2)(v) of SC &
ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 and Sections 4 and 5 of the Immoral Traffic Prevention Act, 1956, subject to the following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum, to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court;
b) The petitioner shall appear regularly on all the dates of hearing before the Trial Court unless the Trial Court exempts his appearance for valid reasons;
c) The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses;
d) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Trial Court without permission of the said Court until the case registered against him is disposed off.
SD/-
(S VISHWAJITH SHETTY) JUDGE NMS Shri Manoj vs State Of Karnataka on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80370321/
